items.title: fresh verifier for G1 item C18

items.title: first G2 runs: far boundary with the relaxed lapse, dust-filled bubble
items.task: The next G2 runs of this track, as the lead named them on 2026-11-21 (HANDOFF.md, stage/REVIEW-wave3.md): ES-1GB (the vacuum-bubble data with the relaxed lapse and the outer faces at 384 M; input built from es_runs/inputs/es1g_dx8.athinput plus the root level of drift_controls/inputs/v1b_bnd384.athinput), its vacuum control V-1GB, then ES-F (dust filling the bubble; flux_tools/inputs/esf_dx8.athinput, command in HANDOFF.md). Use the release executables of core-v0.4. Before each run write its prediction and pass criterion in your journal (for ES-1GB: does the horizon growth of ES-1G, +6.96e-3 over 100-200 M, go away when the boundary is far? what would show that it does not come from the boundary?). Submit through harness/bin/nrpic-run (two jobs of the owner at a time), analyse with the existing scripts (es_runs, drift_controls, flux_tools/esf_analyse.py), look at every figure, and report the horizon-mass drift against the control and, for ES-F, the mass growth against the integrated particle flux through the horizon. Also carry secondary_infall's run to a/a_i = 30 on processors if no other session of this batch does (the package secondary_infall runs beside you: read its journal first). At most three card-hours.

items.title: isolated binary at three member resolutions; input of the next passage
items.task: The first passage run (P1, mass ratio four, members resolved with m/8) did not test the Hills mechanism: its binary merged at t = 48.8 M, before the pericentre (stage/REVIEW-wave3.md; decision 0021 item 7). This package decides the member resolution of the next passage. Read tracks/F-hills/p1 and g2mesh (q = 4 at m/16 fits one card: 3000 slots at 78.8 of 80 GiB), three_punctures/PLAN.md, and coord/INTERFACES/multi_puncture.md with the mass-scaled shift damping of release core-v0.4 (shift_eta_profile; junk_gauge's outcome in nr_first/JOURNAL.md). (1) Prediction first: the inspiral time of the isolated binary of P1 from the post-Newtonian reference (eih) and from the quadrupole formula; what a resolution-driven merger would look like (inspiral time rising steeply with resolution) against a physical one. (2) Runs with the release card executable of core-v0.5: the binary of P1 alone (no third black hole), same separation and momenta, at member resolutions m/8, m/12 and m/16, each to t = 100 M or merger (chains through harness/bin/nrpic-run; at most six card-hours in all; two jobs of the owner at a time; never wait idle: prepare the analysis meanwhile). (3) Analysis: separation and orbital phase against time for the three resolutions and the references; the time to merger or its lower bound; horizon masses; convergence order if any. (4) The verdict: at which resolution the binary survives the 100 M that the passage needs; then the complete input and chain command of the passage P1b at that resolution (do not submit it: the lead decides), with its cost from the measured rates. If the queue does not let the runs finish in your session, leave them running, registered, with the analysis script ready and the exact command to read them.
